title.en: Putting cryptography into the network: IPsec, firewalls, VPNs and HTTPS
title.zh: 把密码学放进网络：IPsec、防火墙、VPN 和 HTTPS

description.en: Work out which layer of the protocol stack each security measure sits in and which properties it covers, and walk through IPsec's two modes, firewalls, VPNs and the TLS handshake.
description.zh: 弄清安全措施放在协议栈的哪一层、各管哪几条性质，并走通 IPsec 的两种模式、防火墙、VPN 和 TLS 握手。

name.en: The five goals of communication security and four kinds of solution
name.zh: 通信安全的五个目标与四类方案 (communication security)
IPsec 与安全关联 (IPsec, Security Association)
传输模式与隧道模式 (transport mode, tunnel mode)

name.en: Where a firewall sits and what it does

name.zh: HTTPS 与 TLS 握手 (TLS handshake)

description.en: Thinking encryption can only be done by each application itself, and not realizing it can sit in a layer below the applications and protect them all at once.
description.zh: 以为加密只能由每个应用自己做，想不到可以放在应用下面的某一层，一次保护所有应用。

description.en: Thinking that once data is encrypted, an attacker cannot resend a recorded packet unchanged. Encryption protects secrecy; it has nothing to say about old versus new.
description.zh: 以为只要加了密，攻击者就没法把录下的包原样重发。加密保的是保密，管不到新旧。

description.en: Thinking an HMAC can recognize a resent packet. An HMAC only proves the content was not altered; an unchanged copy passes just the same.
description.zh: 以为 HMAC 能认出重发的包。HMAC 只证明内容没被改，原封不动的副本照样通过。

description.en: Thinking transport mode also hides the original IP header. In transport mode the IP header is in the clear, so who is talking to whom is plain to see.
description.zh: 以为传输模式也把原 IP 头藏起来了。传输模式的 IP 头是明文，谁在和谁通信一览无余。

description.en: Seeing that the new IP header in tunnel mode is unprotected and concluding that everything inside is exposed. The new IP header holds only the addresses of the two gateways; the real internal addresses are in the old IP header, which is encrypted.
description.zh: 看到隧道模式的新 IP 头不受保护，就以为里面的一切都暴露了。新 IP 头里只有两个网关的地址，真正的内网地址在旧 IP 头里，被加密了。

description.en: Thinking that once a firewall is installed you are secure. It only governs packets entering and leaving at the border: viruses in permitted traffic, insider threats and fake websites are all beyond it.
description.zh: 以为装了防火墙就安全了。它只管边界上进出的包：放行流量里的病毒、内部威胁、假网站，它都管不了。

description.en: Thinking that a server presenting a certificate proves it is the real server. A certificate is public and anyone can copy it; what has to be proven is that it holds the matching private key.
description.zh: 以为服务器出示证书，就证明它是真服务器。证书是公开的，谁都能复制，要证明的是它握着对应的私钥。

description.en: Thinking IPsec or TLS can provide non-repudiation. They use keys shared by both sides, and anyone can produce the same checksum, so they cannot prove who sent something; that takes a digital signature.
description.zh: 以为 IPsec 或 TLS 能提供不可否认性。它们用双方共享的密钥，谁都做得出同样的校验码，证明不了是谁发的，得靠数字签名。

description.en: Mixing up integrity and availability: an HMAC can detect that a packet was altered, but it cannot stop a flood of junk requests from crushing the service.
description.zh: 把完整性和可用性混为一谈：HMAC 能发现包被改过，却挡不住大量垃圾请求把服务压垮。

chapter.en: Which layer to put security in

title.en: Encrypt everything without changing any program?
title.zh: 不改任何程序，怎么全部加密？

prompt.en: A company has three applications sending data over the Internet: the web, email, and an internal bookkeeping program written more than ten years ago, whose source code nobody understands any more. The boss requires all the traffic of the three applications to be encrypted, and not a single program may be changed. Where should the encryption be done?
prompt.zh: 公司有三个应用在互联网上传数据：网页、邮件，还有一个十几年前写的内部记账程序，源码早就没人看得懂了。老板要求三个应用的流量全部加密，而且一个程序都不许改。加密应该做在哪里？

label.en: Let each application do its own encryption
label.zh: 让每个应用自己做加密

feedback.en: That means changing three programs, and nobody can change the bookkeeping one. If each application does it separately, missing one leaves a hole.
feedback.zh: 这要改三个程序，而记账程序谁也改不动。每个应用各做一遍，漏掉一个，就是一个洞。

label.en: At the network layer: after the data is handed to IP and before it leaves the machine, encrypt it uniformly
label.zh: 做在网络层：数据交给 IP 之后、离开本机之前，统一加密

feedback.en: Right. The applications just hand the data down, and a lower layer encrypts it uniformly; none of the three applications will know.
feedback.zh: 对。应用只管把数据交下去，加密由下面的一层统一做，三个应用都不会知道。

label.en: Just install an encryption plug-in in the browser
label.zh: 只在浏览器里装一个加密插件

feedback.en: A plug-in covers only the web pages in the browser; email and the bookkeeping program are still in plaintext.
feedback.zh: 插件只管浏览器里的网页，邮件和记账程序仍然是明文。

label.en: Tighten the firewall at the border
label.zh: 把边界上的防火墙调得更严

feedback.en: A firewall decides which packets may enter or leave; it does not encrypt the packets it lets through. We will see later which properties each measure covers.
feedback.zh: 防火墙决定哪些包能进出，不会把放行的包加密。后面会看到每种措施各管哪几条。

explain.en: The lower you put it, the more applications are protected at once and the less the applications must change. The network layer is the layer all applications share. The cost of doing it this way is on the next page.
explain.zh: 越往下放，一次保护的应用越多，应用要改的越少。网络层正是所有应用共用的那一层。这样做的代价，下一页说。

title.en: At the network layer: protecting all applications at once
title.zh: 放在网络层：一次保护所有应用

text.en: There are two places to put security measures. One is the application layer: each program encrypts its own data. The other is a lower layer, where all programs share one protection. IPsec chooses the latter and sits in the network layer.
text.zh: 安全措施有两种放法。一种放在应用层：每个程序自己加密自己的数据。一种放在下面的层：所有程序共用一套保护。IPsec 选的是后者，放在网络层 (network layer)。

alt.en: The five-layer protocol stack. On the right, three ways of placing security are marked: the application layer does encryption itself; TLS sits between the application layer and the transport layer; IPsec is in the network layer, protecting all the applications above it together.
alt.zh: 五层协议栈。右侧标出三种放法：应用层自己做加密；TLS 夹在应用层与传输层之间；IPsec 在网络层，上面所有应用一起被保护。

caption.en: Security measures can be placed at different positions in the stack.
caption.zh: 安全措施可以放在栈的不同位置。

text.en: At the network layer, encryption happens after the application hands its data to the transport layer and before the IP packet leaves the machine. The applications above know nothing: the web, email and the old bookkeeping program are protected together, without changing a line of code.
text.zh: 放在网络层，加密发生在应用把数据交给传输层之后、IP 包离开本机之前。上面的应用毫不知情：网页、邮件、老记账程序一起被保护，一行代码都不用改。

rows.en: No; configure once on the system or gateway
rows.zh: 不用，在系统或网关上配置一次

rows.en: Miss one application and it is a hole
rows.zh: 漏一个应用，就是一个洞

rows.en: All traffic that goes over IP is covered
rows.zh: 所有走 IP 的流量都在里面

rows.en: Down to one user, one email
rows.zh: 可以细到某个用户、某封邮件

rows.en: Only to machines and gateways; it does not know who is using them
rows.zh: 只到机器和网关，不知道是谁在用

title.en: Beyond the slides: the cost of sitting one layer lower
title.zh: 超出课件：放低一层的代价

body.en: The network layer recognizes only machines (IP addresses); it does not know “who is signing this contract”. If you want an email that can later prove you wrote it, you still need a digital signature at the application layer. So lower is not always better; it depends on what is being protected.
body.zh: 网络层只认得机器（IP 地址），不知道“这是谁在签这份合同”。想要一封事后能证明是你写的邮件，还得在应用层做数字签名。所以安全不是放得越低越好，要看保护的是什么。

title.en: Five goals, four kinds of solution: who covers which
title.zh: 五个目标，四类方案：谁管哪几条

text.en: Lesson 17 (Introduction to network security) listed five properties of security: confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication and non-repudiation. This lesson has four kinds of solution: IPsec, the firewall, the virtual private network (VPN), and Web security, that is, HTTPS.
text.zh: 第 17 课（网络安全入门）列过安全的五个性质：保密性 (confidentiality)、完整性 (integrity)、可用性 (availability)、身份认证 (authentication)、不可否认性 (non-repudiation)。这一课有四类方案：IPsec、防火墙 (firewall)、虚拟专用网 (VPN)，以及 Web 安全，也就是 HTTPS。

text.en: They do not each cover all five; each has its own share of the work.
text.zh: 它们不是各管全部五条，而是各有分工。

rows.en: Partial: blocks traffic that should not come in
rows.zh: 部分：挡掉不该进来的流量

rows.en: Partial: via the firewalls at both ends
✓ only whoever holds the key can compute the HMAC
rows.zh: ✓ 只有握着密钥的人算得出 HMAC

rows.en: Partial: only by address and port
rows.zh: 部分：只能按地址和端口认

text.en: The whole last row is empty. Non-repudiation needs a digital signature. IPsec and TLS protect data with keys shared by both sides: either side can produce the same checksum, so they cannot prove to a third party that “this packet came from the other side”.
text.zh: 最后一行整行是空的。不可否认性要靠数字签名 (digital signature)。IPsec 和 TLS 保护数据用的是双方共享的密钥：两边都做得出同样的校验码，所以向第三方证明不了“这个包是对方发的”。

title.en: Beyond the slides
title.zh: 超出课件

body.en: The slides only list the five goals and four kinds of solution, and do not pair them up; this table is our own arrangement. The next few pages work out, one at a time, why each cell is the way it is.
body.zh: 课件只列出了五个目标和四类方案，没有把它们配对，这张表是我们整理的。每一格为什么是这样，后面几页会逐个弄明白。

chapter.en: IPsec: adding protection at the network layer

title.en: What IPsec gives you: three things
title.zh: IPsec 给你三样东西

text.en: IPsec provides three services. It must process every packet and so must be fast, so all of it is built on symmetric-key cryptography.
text.zh: IPsec 提供三项服务。它要处理每一个包，必须快，所以全部建立在对称密钥 (symmetric-key) 密码学上。

items.en: **Secrecy**: the content of the packet is encrypted, so an eavesdropper cannot read it.
items.zh: **保密**：包的内容被加密，窃听者读不懂。

items.en: **Data integrity**: every packet carries an HMAC, a checksum computed with the shared key. If even one bit of the content is changed, the check fails.
items.zh: **数据完整**：每个包带一个 HMAC，是用共享密钥算出的校验码。内容被改了一个比特，校验就对不上。

items.en: **Replay protection**: blocks old packets that were recorded and resent unchanged.
items.zh: **防重放 (replay protection)**：挡住被录下来、原样重发的旧包。

text.en: Why is the third needed? Suppose you send an encrypted packet: “transfer 100 yuan to B”. The attacker cannot read it and cannot alter it. But he records it and an hour later sends it again unchanged. Not one bit of the packet has changed, the HMAC still checks out, and the bank decrypts it and transfers again. This is a replay attack. Neither encryption nor the HMAC can do anything about it, because it is a perfectly legitimate copy.
text.zh: 第三项为什么需要？设你发出一个加密的包：“转账 100 元给 B”。攻击者读不懂，也改不了。可他把这个包录下来，一小时后原样再发一遍。包一个比特都没变，HMAC 照样对得上，银行解开，又转了一次。这就是重放攻击 (replay attack)。加密和 HMAC 都拿它没办法，因为它是一个完全合法的副本。

text.en: The remedy is to give each packet an increasing sequence number, placed in the part protected by the HMAC, where the attacker cannot change it. The receiver remembers which numbers it has received, and drops any packet whose number was already seen or is too old.
text.zh: 办法是给每个包编一个递增的序号，放在 HMAC 保护的位置，攻击者改不了。接收方记住收过哪些序号，见到收过的或太旧的，直接丢掉。

summary.en: Detail (beyond the slides): how the receiver remembers sequence numbers
summary.zh: 细节（超出课件）：接收方怎么记序号

text.en: Packets can arrive out of order on the network, so the receiver does not just remember “the largest number”; it keeps a sliding window. Unseen numbers inside the window are accepted and marked; numbers already marked, or older than the window, are dropped. Sequence numbers must never be reused, so a new SA (next page) must be set up before they run out.
text.zh: 包在网上可能乱序到达，所以接收方不是只记“最大的序号”，而是维护一个滑动窗口 (window)：窗口里没见过的序号收下并标记，已标记的、或比窗口还旧的，丢弃。序号不能回头重用，快用完之前必须换一个新的 SA（下一页）。

text.en: The range of protection can also be chosen: one TCP connection, all traffic between two hosts, or all traffic between a pair of routers. IPsec is also not tied to one algorithm: the encryption algorithm and the HMAC algorithm can both be changed, as long as the two sides agree beforehand. Where is the agreed information recorded?
text.zh: 保护的范围也可以选：一条 TCP 连接，两台主机之间的所有流量，或者一对路由器之间的所有流量。IPsec 也不绑定某一种算法：加密算法、HMAC 算法都可以换，双方事先约好就行。约好的这些东西，记在哪里？

title.en: What stops a resent packet
title.zh: 重发的包，凭什么被挡下

prompt.en: An attacker records a packet protected by IPsec (its content is “transfer 100 yuan”) and sends it again to the bank an hour later, unchanged. Not one bit of this packet has been modified. What does IPsec use to stop it?
prompt.zh: 攻击者录下了一个被 IPsec 保护的包（内容是“转账 100 元”），一小时后原样再发给银行。这个包没有被改动一个比特。IPsec 靠什么把它挡下？

label.en: Encryption: the attacker cannot understand the packet, so resending it is useless
label.zh: 加密：攻击者看不懂这个包，所以重发也没用

feedback.en: He does not need to understand it, only to resend it unchanged. Encryption protects secrecy; it has nothing to say about whether the packet is old.
feedback.zh: 他根本不需要看懂，只要原样重发。加密保的是保密，管不到“这个包是不是旧的”。

label.en: The HMAC: the check on the resent packet will fail
label.zh: HMAC：重发的包校验会失败

feedback.en: An HMAC checks whether the content was altered. The resent packet is an untouched copy and the check is entirely correct, so this barrier cannot stop it.
feedback.zh: HMAC 检查内容有没有被改。重发的是原封不动的副本，校验完全正确，这一关挡不住它。

label.en: The sequence number: the receiver sees that this number was already received and drops it
label.zh: 序号：接收方发现这个序号已经收过，直接丢弃

feedback.en: Right. The sequence number is unique to each packet, sits within the range the HMAC protects so the attacker cannot change it, and the receiver remembers which ones it has received.
feedback.zh: 对。序号是每个包独有的，放在 HMAC 保护的范围里，攻击者改不了，接收方又记得收过哪些。

label.en: A longer key, so the attacker cannot resend it
label.zh: 换一把更长的密钥，攻击者就没法重发了

feedback.en: Replay does not need to break anything. However long the key, a packet resent unchanged is still a legitimate copy.
feedback.zh: 重放不需要破解任何东西。密钥再长，原样重发的包照样是合法的副本。

hints.en: What must be different about the resent packet compared with the original?
hints.zh: 重发的包和原来那个包，有哪一点一定不同？

explain.en: The answer is the sequence number. The replayed packet has not changed in a single bit, so neither encryption nor the HMAC can do anything about it: it is a perfectly legitimate copy. Only the sequence number, unique to each packet, together with the receiver's memory, can recognize an “old packet”. The sequence number lies within the range protected by the HMAC, so the attacker cannot change it.
explain.zh: 答案是序号。重放的包内容一个比特都没动，所以加密和 HMAC 都拿它没办法，它是一个完全合法的副本。能认出“旧包”的，只有每个包独有的序号，加上接收方的记忆。序号放在 HMAC 保护的范围里，攻击者改不了。

title.en: Security Association (SA): agree first, then communicate
title.zh: 安全关联 (SA)：先约好，再通信

text.en: To use encryption and HMACs, both sides must first agree on three things: which algorithm to use, which key to use, and where the sequence number has got to. So IPsec is connection-oriented: before communicating, it first sets up a “connection”, which in IPsec is called a Security Association (SA).
text.zh: 加密和 HMAC 要用起来，双方得先对三件事看法一致：用哪种算法，用哪把密钥，序号数到几了。所以 IPsec 是面向连接 (connection-oriented) 的：通信之前，先建一条“连接”，它在 IPsec 里叫安全关联 (Security Association, SA)。

text.en: What is stored in an SA
text.zh: 一个 SA 里存着什么

items.en: **Algorithms**: which encryption algorithm and which HMAC algorithm.
items.zh: **算法**：用哪种加密算法，哪种 HMAC 算法。

items.en: **Keys**: one for encryption, one for computing the HMAC.
items.zh: **密钥**：加密用的，算 HMAC 用的。

items.en: **Sequence numbers**: what number has been sent, what number has been received (needed for replay protection).
items.zh: **序号**：发到几号了，收到几号了（防重放要用）。

items.en: **Mode and lifetime**: transport mode or tunnel mode, and how long this SA may be used.
items.zh: **模式与寿命**：传输模式还是隧道模式，这个 SA 能用多久。

items.en: **An identifier (SPI)**: carried in the packet header, and the receiver uses it to find the right SA among many.
items.zh: **一个编号 (SPI)**：包头里带着它，接收方凭它从许多 SA 里找出对的那一个。

text.en: An SA is one-way. Packets from A to B use one SA and packets from B back to A use another, so a round trip needs two.
text.zh: SA 是单向的。A 发给 B 的包用一个 SA，B 回给 A 的包用另一个，所以一来一回要两个。

title.en: Beyond the slides
title.zh: 超出课件

body.en: The slides give only a one-sentence definition of an SA. The list above comes from the IPsec standard, and is there to show what a “connection” really is: an agreement kept jointly by both sides.
body.zh: 课件对 SA 只有一句定义。上面这张清单来自 IPsec 标准，用来说明“连接”到底是什么：一份双方共同保管的约定。

text.en: Two headers
text.zh: 两种头

text.en: The SA also decides which header protects each packet. IPsec has two headers: the Authentication header (AH) and the Encapsulating Security Payload header (ESP header).
text.zh: SA 还决定每个包用哪种头来保护。IPsec 有两种头：认证头 (Authentication header, AH) 和封装安全载荷头 (Encapsulating Security Payload header, ESP 头)。

rows.en: Yes, the last block in the figure

text.en: The slides' figure shows ESP, because it covers everything. AH does authentication only and does not encrypt.
text.zh: 课件的图画的是 ESP，因为它什么都管。AH 只做认证，不加密。

summary.en: Detail (beyond the slides): AH and ESP authenticate different ranges
summary.zh: 细节（超出课件）：AH 与 ESP 认证的范围不一样

text.en: AH's authentication range includes even the fields in the IP header that do not change along the way. ESP authenticates only the part after the ESP header; the IP header is not included.
text.zh: AH 的认证范围连 IP 头里途中不会变的字段也算在内。ESP 只认证 ESP 头之后的部分，IP 头不在里面。

text.en: Where the keys come from
text.zh: 密钥从哪来

text.en: Keys cannot be written in beforehand, nor sent in plaintext. This is the other half of IPsec, key management, handled by ISAKMP (Internet Security Association and Key Management Protocol): the two sides use it to negotiate algorithms, confirm each other's identity, and establish keys, which is to say, to build the SA. So IPsec has two parts: the headers handle each packet, and ISAKMP handles building the SA.
text.zh: 密钥不能事先写死，也不能明文送过去。这是 IPsec 的另一块，密钥管理，由 ISAKMP (Internet Security Association and Key Management Protocol) 负责：双方用它协商算法、确认彼此身份、建立密钥，也就是建出 SA。所以 IPsec 分两块：头管每一个包，ISAKMP 管建 SA。

summary.en: Detail (beyond the slides): how ISAKMP works in practice
summary.zh: 细节（超出课件）：ISAKMP 在实际中怎么做

text.en: ISAKMP is a framework. The protocol actually used to exchange keys is called IKE, which uses Diffie-Hellman (lesson 18) so that the two sides compute the same key without meeting, and then confirms the other side's identity with certificates or a previously agreed key.
text.zh: ISAKMP 是一个框架。真正用来交换密钥的协议叫 IKE，里面用 Diffie-Hellman（第 18 课）让双方不见面也算出同一把密钥，再用证书或事先约好的密钥确认对方的身份。

title.en: Two modes: insert just one header, or wrap the whole packet
title.zh: 两种模式：只插一个头，还是整个包起来

text.en: The same ESP protection can be fitted into a packet in two ways.
text.zh: 同样是 ESP 保护，可以用两种方式装进包里。

items.en: **Transport mode**: the original IP header is left alone and the ESP header is inserted after it. Used for end-to-end communication, for example between your computer and a server.
items.zh: **传输模式 (transport mode)**：原 IP 头不动，在它后面插入 ESP 头。用在端到端通信，比如你的电脑和服务器之间。

items.en: **Tunnel mode**: the whole original packet (the old IP header included) is sealed as cargo and a new IP header is put around the outside. Used between gateways, for example security gateways and company firewalls.
items.zh: **隧道模式 (tunnel mode)**：把整个原包（旧 IP 头也算在内）当作货物封起来，外面再套一个新 IP 头。用在网关之间，比如安全网关、公司防火墙。

alt.en: The structure of the two kinds of ESP packet. Transport mode: IP header, ESP header, TCP header, payload plus padding, HMAC; the authenticated range runs from the ESP header to the payload, and the encrypted range from the TCP header to the payload. Tunnel mode: new IP header, ESP header, old IP header, TCP header, payload plus padding, HMAC; the authenticated range runs from the ESP header to the payload, the encrypted range from the old IP header to the payload, and the new IP header lies outside both ranges.
alt.zh: 两种 ESP 包的结构。传输模式：IP 头、ESP 头、TCP 头、载荷加填充、HMAC，认证范围从 ESP 头到载荷，加密范围从 TCP 头到载荷。隧道模式：新 IP 头、ESP 头、旧 IP 头、TCP 头、载荷加填充、HMAC，认证范围从 ESP 头到载荷，加密范围从旧 IP 头到载荷，新 IP 头在两个范围之外。

caption.en: The two modes of ESP. The blue bracket is the authenticated range and the red bracket is the encrypted range.
caption.zh: ESP 的两种模式。蓝括号是认证范围，红括号是加密范围。

text.en: Each packet carries two brackets: the authenticated range is the part the HMAC covers, and the encrypted range is the part an eavesdropper cannot read. The HMAC itself is placed at the end.
text.zh: 每个包上有两道括号：认证范围 (authenticated) 是 HMAC 管得到的部分，加密范围 (encrypted) 是窃听者读不懂的部分。HMAC 本身收在最后。

title.en: Three details, and why tunnel mode exists
title.zh: 三个细节，和隧道模式为什么存在

text.en: The figure has three details, and each has a reason.
text.zh: 图里有三个细节，每一个都有原因。

items.en: **The HMAC is outside both ranges.** It is the result computed over the authenticated range and cannot count itself in, so it goes at the end.
items.zh: **HMAC 在两个范围之外。** 它是对认证范围算出来的结果，不能把自己也算进去，所以放在最后。

items.en: **The ESP header is authenticated but not encrypted.** The receiver must read the SPI and the sequence number in the header first, to know which SA's key to decrypt with. If the header were encrypted too, it would be a chicken-and-egg problem: without the key the header cannot be read, and without reading the header the key cannot be found. The header only needs to be protected from tampering, so authentication is enough.
items.zh: **ESP 头被认证，但没有加密。** 接收方要先读头里的 SPI 和序号，才知道该用哪个 SA 的密钥去解密。头也加密，就成了先有鸡还是先有蛋：没有密钥读不了头，不读头找不到密钥。头只要不被篡改就行，所以认证就够。

items.en: **In tunnel mode, the new IP header is outside both ranges.** Routers must read it to forward the packet, so it cannot be encrypted. Routers along the way also change some of its fields, such as the TTL, which decreases by one at every hop, so it cannot go in the authenticated range either.
items.zh: **隧道模式里，新 IP 头在两个范围之外。** 路由器要读它才能转发，所以不能加密。途中的路由器还会改其中的字段，比如每过一跳就减一的 TTL，所以也放不进认证范围。

text.en: So why have tunnel mode
text.zh: 那为什么要有隧道模式

text.en: Take two offices, London and Paris. The computers inside do not understand IPsec, and nobody wants to go and change them one by one. Let the **gateways** at both sides do it for them: computers send packets as usual, the London gateway seals the whole packet into ESP, puts a new IP header around it with the two gateways as addresses, and sends it onto the Internet. At Paris, the gateway opens it and puts the original packet back into the internal network.
text.zh: 设伦敦和巴黎两个办公室，里面的电脑都不懂 IPsec，也没人想一台台去改。让两边的网关 (gateway) 代劳：电脑照常发包，伦敦的网关把整个包封进 ESP，套上一个新 IP 头，地址是两个网关，送上互联网。到了巴黎，网关拆开，把原包放回内网。

items.en: The internal computers do not need to understand IPsec; the gateways do it for them.
items.zh: 内网电脑不用懂 IPsec，网关替它们做。

items.en: An eavesdropper cannot see the real addresses and ports inside: the old IP header and TCP header are within the encrypted range, so he knows only that “two gateways are communicating”, and cannot tell which two computers.
items.zh: 窃听者看不到内网真正的地址和端口：旧 IP 头和 TCP 头都在加密范围里，他只知道“两个网关在通信”，分不出是哪两台电脑。

text.en: Transport mode cannot do either: the original IP header is in the clear, so who is talking to whom is plain to see, and every computer must support IPsec itself.
text.zh: 传输模式做不到这两点：原 IP 头是明文，谁和谁在通信一览无余，而且每台电脑得自己支持 IPsec。

title.en: Between two gateways, which mode to choose
title.zh: 两个网关之间，该选哪种模式

prompt.en: Offices in Melbourne and Beijing each have a security gateway, and the internal computers do not understand IPsec. You set up IPsec between the two gateways, and you want an eavesdropper on the line between the gateways to be unable to tell which computer in an office is talking to which. Which mode should you use? What can the eavesdropper see?
prompt.zh: 墨尔本和北京的两个办公室各有一个安全网关，内网电脑都不懂 IPsec。你在两个网关之间建 IPsec，希望窃听者在两个网关之间的线路上，看不出办公室里哪台电脑在和哪台电脑通信。该用哪种模式？窃听者能看到什么？

label.en: Transport mode; the eavesdropper sees only ciphertext and no address at all
label.zh: 传输模式；窃听者只看到密文，看不到任何地址

feedback.en: Transport mode only inserts the ESP header after the original IP header, and the original IP header is still in the clear, so the addresses are plain to see. Also, the internal computers would have to understand IPsec themselves, which the question says they do not.
feedback.zh: 传输模式只在原 IP 头后面插入 ESP 头，原 IP 头仍是明文，地址一览无余。而且内网电脑得自己懂 IPsec，题里它们不懂。

label.en: Tunnel mode; the eavesdropper sees only the addresses of the two gateways, not the addresses and ports of the internal computers
label.zh: 隧道模式；窃听者只能看到两个网关的地址，看不到内网电脑的地址和端口

feedback.en: Right. The old IP header, TCP header and payload are all sealed within the encrypted range, leaving only the new IP header outside, which holds only the addresses of the two gateways.
feedback.zh: 对。旧 IP 头、TCP 头和载荷都被封进加密范围，外面只剩新 IP 头，里面只有两个网关的地址。

label.en: Tunnel mode; the new IP header is not encrypted, so the eavesdropper can see everything
label.zh: 隧道模式；新 IP 头没有加密，所以窃听者什么都能看到

feedback.en: The new IP header is indeed outside the protection, but it holds only the addresses of the two gateways. The real internal addresses are in the old IP header, sealed within the encrypted range.
feedback.zh: 新 IP 头确实在保护之外，但里面只有两个网关的地址。真正的内网地址在旧 IP 头里，被封进了加密范围。

label.en: Transport mode; the eavesdropper can see the whole content, because ESP only authenticates and does not encrypt
label.zh: 传输模式；窃听者能看到全部内容，因为 ESP 只认证不加密

feedback.en: ESP both authenticates and encrypts: the TCP header and payload are in the encrypted range. What transport mode exposes is the IP header, not the content.
feedback.zh: ESP 既认证又加密：TCP 头和载荷都在加密范围里。传输模式暴露的是 IP 头，不是内容。

hints.en: In which IP header is the real address of the internal computer written? Where is that header sealed?
hints.zh: 内网电脑真正的地址写在哪个 IP 头里？这个头被封在哪里？

explain.en: Tunnel mode seals the old IP header, TCP header and payload as a whole into the encrypted range, so the eavesdropper sees only the new IP header: the addresses of the two gateways. The internal addresses and ports are hidden, and the gateways also do all the work for computers that do not understand IPsec. In transport mode the IP header is in the clear, and every host must itself support IPsec.
explain.zh: 隧道模式把旧 IP 头、TCP 头和载荷整体封进加密范围，窃听者只看得到新 IP 头：两个网关的地址。内网的地址和端口藏起来了，网关还替不懂 IPsec 的电脑做了全部工作。传输模式的 IP 头是明文，也要求每台主机自己支持 IPsec。

title.en: The firewall: a door at the border
title.zh: 防火墙：边界上的一道门

text.en: IPsec protects packets on the road. Another danger is packets that should not come in at all. A firewall leaves only a controlled set of passages between the internal network and the outside, like a building with a single entrance and a guard at the door.
text.zh: IPsec 保护的是路上的包。另一类危险是：不该进来的包，根本不该进来。防火墙 (firewall) 的做法，是在内网和外网之间只留一组受控的通路，像一栋楼只开一个大门，门口有保安。

text.en: An ideal firewall has three properties
text.zh: 理想的防火墙有三条

items.en: **All traffic in and out must pass through it.** If one computer sets up its own phone hotspot to get online, it bypasses this door.
items.zh: **所有进出的流量都必须经过它。** 要是有一台电脑自己开了手机热点上网，就绕开了这道门。

items.en: **Only authorized traffic may pass.** Deny by default; let through only what the rules explicitly allow.
items.zh: **只有被授权的流量能通过。** 默认拒绝，规则明说可以的才放。

items.en: **It must not itself be breached.** Everyone goes through this door; once it is breached, there is no second line of defense inside.
items.zh: **它自己不能被攻破。** 所有人都从这道门过，门一被攻破，里面就没有第二道防线了。

text.en: How it decides: the packet filter
text.zh: 它怎么决定：包过滤 (packet filter)

text.en: The firewall looks at the header of each packet, checks it against a table of rules, and decides to allow or deny. The rules are written by address, port and protocol. Real rules use IP addresses or address ranges; here names stand in for them.
text.zh: 防火墙看每个包的头，对照一张规则表，决定放行还是拒绝。规则按地址、端口、协议来写。实际规则里写的是 IP 地址或地址段，这里用名字代替。

text.en: The rules are searched from top to bottom, and the first one that matches takes effect. The last rule denies everything, which is what “only authorized traffic may pass” means.
text.zh: 规则从上往下找，第一条符合的生效。最后一条拒绝一切，这就是“只有被授权的流量才能通过”。

summary.en: Detail (beyond the slides): what about returning packets, and what kinds of firewall are there
summary.zh: 细节（超出课件）：回来的包怎么办，防火墙有哪几种

text.en: Rule 3 only allows connections started from the inside going out. A website's reply packets are in the “in” direction, and under this table they would be denied by rule 4. So a simple packet filter also needs a rule to allow replies, or else a stateful firewall: it remembers which connections were started from the inside and automatically allows the matching reply packets. Going further up, an application gateway also reads the content of the application layer, which is where the limits discussed below come from.
text.zh: 第 3 条只放行内网向外发起的连接。网站的回包是“进”方向，按这张表会被第 4 条拒绝。所以简单的包过滤还要多一条放行回包的规则，或者用有状态防火墙 (stateful firewall)：它记得哪些连接是内网发起的，自动放行对应的回包。再往上，应用层网关 (application gateway) 还会读应用层的内容，下面讲的局限就从这里来。

title.en: Where to put the Web and mail servers
title.zh: Web 和邮件服务器放在哪里

text.en: There is a contradiction here. A firewall wants to keep outsiders out, yet the company's website and mail server are there precisely so that outsiders can reach them. The best firewall is not one that cuts everything off from the Internet.
text.zh: 这里有个矛盾。防火墙想把外人挡在外面，可公司的网站和邮件服务器，偏偏就是要让外人来访问。最好的防火墙，不是把一切都和互联网断开。

text.en: Put them inside the internal network? Then outside access to the website goes straight through into the internal network. Once the website is breached, the attacker is already inside. Put them outside the firewall, unprotected? That is running naked.
text.zh: 放进内网？那外人对网站的访问，就直接通到内网里。网站一旦被攻破，攻击者已经站在内网了。放到防火墙外面、不设防？那等于裸奔。

text.en: The compromise: give these servers, which must face outward, a separate zone between the Internet and the internal network. It is called the demilitarized zone (DMZ). The slides' figure draws this structure but does not give it a name.
text.zh: 折中的办法：给这些必须对外的服务器单独一块区域，夹在互联网和内网之间。它叫非军事区 (DMZ, demilitarized zone)。课件的图画出了这个结构，没有给它起名字。

caption.en: The servers sit in a separate zone between the firewall and the border.
caption.zh: 服务器放在防火墙和边界之间的一块单独区域。

text.en: The Internet can reach only the DMZ, and only the ports used for Web and mail. The internal network hides behind the firewall, out of the Internet's reach. Even if the website in the DMZ is breached, a firewall still stands before the attacker.
text.zh: 互联网只能到 DMZ，而且只能碰 Web 和邮件用的端口。内网藏在防火墙后面，互联网到不了。就算 DMZ 里的网站被攻破，攻击者面前还有一道防火墙。

title.en: Three things a firewall cannot handle
title.zh: 防火墙管不到的三件事

text.en: A firewall stands at the border and sees only the packets going in and out. This determines three limits.
text.zh: 防火墙站在边界上，看的只是进出的包。这决定了它的三个局限。

items.en: **To look at the higher layers, it breaks layering.** A router should read only the IP header. But to tell “ordinary HTTP” from “HTTP used by P2P”, which may use the same port, the IP header and TCP header show no difference; only by reading the application-layer content can they be told apart. So the firewall must look at transport-layer and application-layer information, which breaks the usual rule of protocol layering: each layer should handle only its own header. The cost is that it is slower, it must understand every application, and once the content is encrypted by HTTPS it can see nothing at all.
items.zh: **要看高层，就违反了分层。** 路由器本来只该读 IP 头。可要分辨“普通 HTTP”和“P2P 用的 HTTP”，两者都可能走同一个端口，从 IP 头和 TCP 头看不出区别，只有读到应用层的内容才分得出来。于是防火墙得去看传输层和应用层的信息，违反了协议分层的常规：每一层本来只管自己的头。代价是更慢，要懂每一种应用，而且内容一旦被 HTTPS 加密，它就什么也看不见了。

items.en: **What is let through may be poisoned.** An email is allowed by the rules, and a virus in the attachment comes in with it. A firewall asks “may this packet go through?”, not “is what is in the packet any good?”.
items.zh: **放行的东西里可以有毒。** 邮件被规则放行了，附件里的病毒也跟着进来。防火墙问的是“这个包能不能走”，不是“包里的东西好不好”。

items.en: **It cannot handle inhouse threats.** A firewall guards the door. People already inside the building, such as an employee carrying a virus-infected USB stick, an infected laptop plugged into the internal network, or an insider who wants to steal data, do not have to go through that door.
items.zh: **管不了内部威胁 (inhouse threats)。** 防火墙守在门口。已经在楼里的人，比如带着中毒 U 盘的员工、接进内网的被感染的笔记本、想偷数据的内部人员，不用经过那道门。

text.en: So a firewall is just one layer. It blocks what “should not come in”; other dangers have to be handled by IPsec, TLS, antivirus software and internal permissions.
text.zh: 所以防火墙只是一层。它挡的是“不该进来的”，别的危险要靠 IPsec、TLS、杀毒软件和内部权限去管。

title.en: Which of these can this firewall stop
title.zh: 这台防火墙挡得住哪一件

prompt.en: A company installs a packet-filtering firewall at its network border, with these rules: allow traffic to the Web server on port 443 and to the mail server on port 25, allow outbound traffic from the internal network on ports 80 and 443, and deny everything else. Which of the following can this firewall stop?
prompt.zh: 一家公司在网络边界上装了一台包过滤防火墙，规则是：放行去 Web 服务器 443 端口和邮件服务器 25 端口的流量，放行内网向外的 80、443 端口流量，其余全部拒绝。下面哪一件事，这台防火墙能挡住？

label.en: Someone outside starts a connection to port 3306 of a database server in the internal network
label.zh: 外部有人向内网一台数据库服务器的 3306 端口发起连接

feedback.en: Right. The destination and port of this connection are in none of the allow rules, and the last rule, “deny everything”, blocks it.
feedback.zh: 对。这个连接的目的地和端口不在任何放行规则里，最后一条“拒绝一切”把它挡下。

label.en: An employee receives an email with a virus hidden in the attachment
label.zh: 员工收到一封邮件，附件里藏着病毒

feedback.en: The email travels over the allowed port 25, and the rules cannot see what is in the attachment. This is limit two: allowed traffic may also be poisoned.
feedback.zh: 邮件走的是被放行的 25 端口，规则看不出附件里有什么。这是局限之二：放行的流量也可能有毒。

label.en: An employee's infected laptop joins the internal network and spreads the virus to other computers
label.zh: 员工带来的中毒笔记本接入内网，向其他电脑传播病毒

feedback.en: These packets flow only inside the internal network and never pass the firewall at the border. This is limit three: it cannot handle inhouse threats.
feedback.zh: 这些包只在内网里流动，从不经过边界上的防火墙。这是局限之三：管不了内部威胁。

label.en: Someone disguises P2P traffic as ordinary web access and sends it out through port 443
label.zh: 有人把 P2P 程序的流量伪装成普通网页访问，从 443 端口出去

feedback.en: A packet filter looks only at addresses, ports and protocols. To tell whether the traffic is web pages or P2P, it would have to read the application-layer content, which this firewall's rule table cannot do. This is limit one.
feedback.zh: 包过滤只看地址、端口、协议。要认出流量里装的是网页还是 P2P，得读应用层的内容，这台防火墙的规则表做不到。这是局限之一。

hints.en: First ask: would the packets in this case pass through the border? If so, is there a line in the rule table that allows them?
hints.zh: 先问：这件事里的包，会不会经过边界？经过的话，规则表上有没有放行它的那一行？

explain.en: A packet-filtering firewall works only on traffic that “crosses the border and can be told apart by address and port”. Only a fits: the destination port is not on the allow list, and default deny stops it. b is poison in allowed traffic, c is an inhouse threat, and d needs reading application-layer content.
explain.zh: 包过滤防火墙只对“经过边界、而且按地址和端口就能区分”的流量起作用。只有 a 满足：目的端口不在放行名单上，被默认拒绝挡住。b 是放行流量里的毒，c 是内部威胁，d 要读应用层的内容。

chapter.en: VPN: borrow public lines to build a private network
chapter.zh: VPN：借公共线路，造一张私网

title.en: VPN: a private network without leasing lines
title.zh: VPN：不租专线，也能有一张私网

text.en: The London and Paris offices want to reach each other's internal systems, and the data must not be seen by outsiders. The most direct way is to lease lines and build a physical private network: the lines belong only to you. But every pair of locations that need secure communication needs one, which is very expensive.
text.zh: 伦敦和巴黎的办公室要互相访问内部系统，数据不能让外人看到。最直接的办法是租专线，建一张物理专用网 (physical private network)：线只属于你。可是每两个需要安全通信的地点都要租一条，很贵。

text.en: Another way: keep using the public Internet for the lines, and build a “virtual” private network on top of it. This is the Virtual Private Network (VPN): a virtual network layer built on an IP network, providing secure end-to-end connections over public facilities.
text.zh: 另一个办法：线路照用公共的互联网，在上面做一张“虚拟”的私网。这就是虚拟专用网 (Virtual Private Network, VPN)：建在 IP 网络上的一层虚拟网络，在公共设施上提供安全的端到端连接。

text.en: A common approach is: put a firewall at each end of every connection, and then, between all pairs of endpoints, build IPsec tunnels using security associations (SA).
text.zh: 常见的做法是：每个连接的两端各放一个防火墙，再在所有端点对之间，用安全关联 (SA) 建立 IPsec 隧道。

alt.en: Four endpoints: the London office, the Paris office, at home, and on a trip, with an IPsec tunnel across the Internet between every pair, six in all.
alt.zh: 四个端点：伦敦办公室、巴黎办公室、在家、出差，两两之间都有一条穿过互联网的 IPsec 隧道，一共六条。

caption.en: Tunnels are built between all pairs of endpoints.
caption.zh: 所有端点对之间都建隧道。

text.en: How a VPN relates to IPsec tunnel mode
text.zh: VPN 和 IPsec 隧道模式是什么关系

text.en: A VPN is the goal: let people scattered in different places act as if they were on one private network. IPsec tunnel mode is one way of doing it: the office gateway is the security gateway described earlier, both a firewall and an endpoint of the tunnel, sealing the internal packets into ESP and sending them across the Internet.
text.zh: VPN 是目的：让分散在各处的人，像在同一张私网里。IPsec 隧道模式是其中一种做法：办公室的网关就是前面说的安全网关，既是防火墙，又是隧道的端点，把内网的包封进 ESP，穿过互联网。

text.en: It is transparent to the end user: a person in London visiting a server in Paris sees no difference from visiting a local server, and does not need to care how the packets are put into the tunnel. Tunnels can also be set up on demand: the SA is built only when it is needed.
text.zh: 对终端用户是透明的 (transparent)：伦敦的人访问巴黎的服务器，和访问本地的服务器没有区别，包怎样被装进隧道，他不用管。隧道还可以按需 (on demand) 建立，用到的时候才建 SA。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: a VPN does not have to use IPsec
summary.zh: 超出课件：VPN 不一定用 IPsec

text.en: There are also VPNs that use TLS for the tunnel. The slides cover the kind that uses IPsec.
text.zh: 也有用 TLS 做隧道的 VPN。课件讲的是用 IPsec 的这一种。

title.en: With more endpoints, how fast do tunnels grow
title.zh: 端点越多，隧道涨得多快

intro.en: “Build tunnels between all pairs of endpoints” sounds neat; what is the cost? With $n$ endpoints, count how many tunnels must be built.
intro.zh: “所有端点对之间建隧道”听着整齐，代价是什么？设有 $n$ 个端点，数一数要建多少条隧道。

why.en: Each of the $n$ endpoints must connect to each of the other $n-1$, so first count them once per endpoint.
why.zh: $n$ 个端点，每个都要和其余 $n-1$ 个各连一条，先各数一遍。

why.en: A tunnel has two endpoints and was counted once from each end, so divide by 2.
why.zh: 一条隧道有两个端点，被两头各数了一次，所以除以 2。

why.en: London, Paris, at home and on a trip from the slides' figure: 4 endpoints, 6 tunnels, exactly the 6 thick lines in the figure.
why.zh: 课件图里的伦敦、巴黎、在家、出差：4 个端点，6 条隧道，正是图里那 6 条粗线。

why.en: From 4 endpoints to 10, tunnels grow from 6 to 45.
why.zh: 端点从 4 个到 10 个，隧道从 6 条涨到 45 条。

why.en: Endpoints times 10, tunnels roughly times 100: it grows as $n^2$.
why.zh: 端点乘 10，隧道数约乘 100：它随 $n^2$ 增长。

outro.en: Each new site must build one tunnel to every existing site: the $n$-th site builds $n-1$ new ones. An SA is one-way, so each tunnel needs two, $n(n-1)$ in all. That is why tunnels should be set up on demand, rather than building all of them at the start.
outro.zh: 每多一个站点，就要和所有已有的站点各建一条：第 $n$ 个站点要新建 $n-1$ 条。SA 是单向的，每条隧道要两个，总共 $n(n-1)$ 个。所以隧道要能按需建立，不必一开始把所有的都建好。

title.en: Two more sites, how many more tunnels
title.zh: 再开两个站点，隧道多几条

prompt.en: A company has 6 sites, with IPsec tunnels already built between every pair. Now 2 new sites open, and the new sites also need to connect with every site pairwise. How many more tunnels are there in total?
prompt.zh: 一家公司有 6 个站点，已经在所有站点两两之间建好了 IPsec 隧道。现在又新开 2 个站点，新站点也要和所有站点两两互通。隧道总数一共多出多少条？

hints.en: How many sites must the 7th site build tunnels to? And the 8th?
hints.zh: 第 7 个站点要和几个站点建隧道？第 8 个呢？

explain.en: 6 sites need $\frac{6\times 5}{2}=15$ tunnels, and 8 sites need $\frac{8\times 7}{2}=28$, so there are $28-15=13$ more. You can also count it like this: the 7th site builds one to each of the original 6, and the 8th site builds one to each of the previous 7, $6+7=13$.
explain.zh: 6 个站点要 $\frac{6\times 5}{2}=15$ 条，8 个站点要 $\frac{8\times 7}{2}=28$ 条，多出 $28-15=13$ 条。也可以这样数：第 7 个站点要和原来的 6 个各建一条，第 8 个站点要和前面的 7 个各建一条，$6+7=13$。

chapter.en: HTTPS: adding TLS to the web

title.en: Why use a public key first, then switch to symmetric encryption
title.zh: 为什么先用公钥，再换对称加密

text.en: HTTPS is a secure HTTP: HTTP requests and web pages are first handed to Transport Layer Security (TLS) for encryption, and then to TCP for delivery. TLS sits between HTTP and TCP.
text.zh: HTTPS 是安全的 HTTP：HTTP 的请求和网页，先交给传输层安全 (Transport Layer Security, TLS) 加密，再交给 TCP 去送。TLS 夹在 HTTP 和 TCP 之间。

text.en: The difficulty: you and www.unimelb.edu.au are strangers, with no key agreed beforehand, and someone on the line is listening. To encrypt, both sides must first have the same key, but how can that key be sent over? The two kinds of cryptography from lesson 18 (Symmetric and public-key cryptography, digital signatures and authentication) each have one shortcoming here.
text.zh: 难处在于：你和 www.unimelb.edu.au 是陌生人，事先没有约好的密钥，而线路上有人在听。要加密，双方得先有同一把密钥，可这把密钥怎么送过去？第 18 课（对称与公钥密码、数字签名和认证）里的两种密码，正好各有一样短处。

rows.en: Fast, suitable for large amounts of data
Much slower, unsuitable for large amounts of data
rows.zh: 慢很多，不适合大量数据

rows.en: Both sides must already hold the same one; how to send it is the problem
rows.zh: 双方要先有同一把，怎么送是难题

rows.en: The public key can be made public, no need to meet first
rows.zh: 公钥可以公开，不用先见面

text.en: TLS uses each kind of cryptography where it fits best: **the public key does just one small job, safely agreeing on a symmetric key. After that, the web pages, images and scripts are all encrypted with that symmetric key.** The slow one is used only once, and the fast one is used all the way through. It is like using a safe to pass over one small key first, and then putting all the goods into boxes locked with that key.
text.zh: TLS 把两种密码用在最合适的地方：**公钥只做一件小事，安全地约定一把对称密钥。之后的网页、图片、脚本，全用这把对称密钥加密。** 慢的只用一次，快的用到底。像先用保险柜递一把小钥匙，之后的货都装进用这把钥匙锁的箱子。

text.en: This key is used only within this connection, and is called the session key.
text.zh: 这把密钥只在这次连接里用，叫会话密钥 (session key)。

title.en: The TLS handshake: the six steps at a glance
title.zh: TLS 握手：六步全景

text.en: The TLS handshake happens after the TCP three-way handshake (lesson 12) and before the HTTP request. It has two things to accomplish: negotiate how data will be exchanged securely, and safely establish the session key.
text.zh: TLS 握手 (TLS handshake) 发生在 TCP 三次握手（第 12 课）之后、HTTP 请求之前。它要办成两件事：协商怎样安全地交换数据，并把会话密钥安全地建起来。

alt.en: Timing of the TLS handshake between browser and server: Client Hello, Server Hello, Client Key Exchange, Client Finished, Server Finished, and finally a two-way data exchange.
alt.zh: 浏览器与服务器之间的 TLS 握手时序：Client Hello，Server Hello，Client Key Exchange，Client Finished，Server Finished，最后是双向的数据交换。

caption.en: The first five messages use a public key to work out the session key; from step six, data is sent with the symmetric key.
caption.zh: 前五条消息用公钥谈出会话密钥，第六步开始用对称密钥传数据。

text.en: The first two steps are mutual introductions. **Client Hello**: the browser reports the TLS versions it supports, its list of encryption algorithms, and its data compression methods. **Server Hello**: the server reports the algorithms it chose from the list, a Session ID, and its digital certificate, which carries the server's public key.
text.zh: 前两步是互相介绍。**Client Hello**：浏览器报上自己支持的 TLS 版本、加密算法清单、数据压缩方法。**Server Hello**：服务器报上从清单里选定的算法、一个会话 ID (Session ID)、它的数字证书 (digital certificate)，证书里带着服务器的公钥。

text.en: The Session ID is the name of this handshake. When connecting again later, reporting it lets the two sides reuse the keys already worked out and skip the public-key step.
text.zh: 会话 ID 是这次握手的名字。下次再连时报上它，双方可以直接沿用已经算好的密钥，省掉公钥那一步。

summary.en: Detail (beyond the slides): the random numbers in the two Hellos
summary.zh: 细节（超出课件）：两条 Hello 里的随机数

text.en: Each of the two Hellos also carries a random number (nonce). They take part in the later computation of the session key, ensuring that when the same two parties shake hands again, the key they compute is different.
text.zh: 两条 Hello 里还各带一个随机数 (nonce)。它们会参与后面会话密钥的计算，保证同样的两个人再握手一次，算出的密钥也不一样。

title.en: How the certificate is checked and where the session key comes from
title.zh: 证书怎么验，会话密钥怎么来

text.en: Check the certificate first
text.zh: 先验证书

text.en: The server's public key arrives inside the certificate. Lesson 18 covered certificates: a sentence signed by a Certification Authority (CA), “this name goes with this public key”. The browser checks three things.
text.zh: 服务器的公钥放在证书里一起发来。第 18 课讲过证书：认证机构 (CA) 签了名的一句话，“这个名字对应这把公钥”。浏览器要检查三件事。

items.en: **Signature**: verify the signature on the certificate with a built-in CA public key, following the certificate chain if necessary to a CA it trusts.
items.zh: **签名**：用内置的 CA 公钥验证证书上的签名，必要时顺着证书链找到一个它信任的 CA。

items.en: **Name**: the domain name on the certificate must match the www.unimelb.edu.au you are visiting.
items.zh: **名字**：证书上的域名，要和你访问的 www.unimelb.edu.au 一致。

items.en: **Validity**: it has not expired and has not been revoked.
items.zh: **有效期**：没有过期，也没有被吊销。

text.en: Only when all three pass does the browser believe that this public key really belongs to www.unimelb.edu.au.
text.zh: 三项都通过，浏览器才相信：这把公钥确实属于 www.unimelb.edu.au。

text.en: What is sent in Client Key Exchange
text.zh: Client Key Exchange 里发什么

text.en: The browser randomly generates a secret, called the pre-master secret, encrypts it with the server public key it has just received, and sends it. An eavesdropper who gets the ciphertext can do nothing with it; only the server holding the private key can decrypt it.
text.zh: 浏览器随机生成一串秘密，叫预主密钥 (pre-master secret)，用刚拿到的服务器公钥加密，发过去。窃听者拿到密文也没用，只有握着私钥的服务器解得开。

text.en: Now both sides have the pre-master secret: the browser generated it, and the server decrypted it. Each side uses the same method to compute the master secret from it and the random numbers in the two Hellos, and then derives a set of session keys, used for encryption and integrity checks. The session keys themselves never travel along the line; what travels is only the raw material, encrypted with the public key.
text.zh: 这样双方都有了预主密钥：浏览器自己生成的，服务器解出来的。两边各自用同样的方法，把它和两条 Hello 里的随机数算成主密钥，再导出一组会话密钥，用来加密和做完整性校验。会话密钥自己从没在线路上走过，走过线路的，只有以公钥加密的原料。

text.en: The slides' six steps correspond to earlier TLS versions. TLS 1.3 no longer encrypts a pre-master secret with the server public key and sends it over; it uses Diffie-Hellman: each side sends one half and both compute the same key, and the handshake shrinks to one round trip. The idea has not changed: first agree on a key safely, then switch to symmetric encryption.
text.zh: 课件的六步对应较早的 TLS 版本。TLS 1.3 不再把预主密钥用服务器公钥加密发过去，而是用 Diffie-Hellman：双方各发一半，算出同一把密钥，握手也缩成一个往返。思路没变：先安全地约定密钥，再换成对称加密。

title.en: The two Finished messages: why they are a must
title.zh: 两个 Finished：为什么非有不可

text.en: The keys are computed. But the browser still has two doubts: did the server really compute the same key? And more important, is the other side really www.unimelb.edu.au?
text.zh: 钥匙算好了。可浏览器还有两个疑问：服务器真的算出了同一把密钥吗？更要紧的，对面真的是 www.unimelb.edu.au 吗？

title.en: A certificate is not an identity
title.zh: 证书不等于身份

body.en: A certificate is public: anyone can download a copy and send it to you unchanged. A certificate only says “this public key belongs to this name”; it does not prove that whoever sends the certificate holds the matching private key.
body.zh: 证书是公开的，谁都能下载一份，原样发给你。证书只说“这把公钥属于这个名字”，不证明发证书的人握着对应的私钥。

text.en: There is only one proof of holding the private key: being able to decrypt Client Key Exchange. An impostor cannot decrypt the pre-master secret, so cannot compute the session key, and so cannot produce a message correctly protected with the session key.
text.zh: 握着私钥的证据只有一个：能解开 Client Key Exchange。假冒者解不开预主密钥，就算不出会话密钥，也就造不出一条用会话密钥正确保护的消息。

text.en: **Finished** is that test. Each side uses the key it has just computed to compute a check value over “all the messages in the handshake so far”, and sends it to the other side protected with the session key. The other side computes one too, and only if they match does it pass. When they match, three things are established:
text.zh: **Finished** 就是这道检验。每一方用刚算出的密钥，对“握手里到目前为止的所有消息”算出一个校验值，用会话密钥保护着发给对方。对方自己也算一个，对得上才算过关。对上了，说明三件事：

items.en: Both sides computed the same session key. If the keys differed, decryption would fail or the values would not match.
items.zh: 两边算出了同一把会话密钥。钥匙不同，就解不开或对不上。

items.en: The server really holds the private key. Without the private key there is no session key, and it cannot produce a correct Server Finished.
items.zh: 服务器真的握着私钥。没有私钥就没有会话密钥，做不出正确的 Server Finished。

items.en: The handshake was not tampered with on the way. The check value covers all the messages, so even if someone edits the algorithm list in Client Hello down to only weak algorithms, the check values computed by the two sides will differ.
items.zh: 握手没有被中途篡改。校验值覆盖了所有消息，哪怕有人把 Client Hello 的算法清单改得只剩弱算法，两边算出的校验值也不一样。

text.en: Why both are needed: Server Finished lets the browser confirm the other side is the real server; Client Finished lets the server confirm that the browser side has the same key and has not seen a tampered handshake. Once both pass, we move to step six: data exchange, all encrypted with the session key and carrying an integrity check.
text.zh: 为什么两个都要：Server Finished 让浏览器确认对面是真的服务器；Client Finished 让服务器确认浏览器这边拿到的是同一把钥匙，也没有看到被改过的握手。两个都过了，进入第六步：数据交换，全部用会话密钥加密，并带完整性校验。

title.en: A fake server with a real certificate: where does it give itself away
title.zh: 拿着真证书的假服务器，在哪里露馅

prompt.en: Someone copies the real certificate of www.unimelb.edu.au (certificates are public anyway), sets up a fake server, and sends that certificate to your browser during the TLS handshake. The certificate's signature, domain name and validity period are all fine. Where will this handshake finally give itself away?
prompt.zh: 有人复制了 www.unimelb.edu.au 的真实证书（证书本来就是公开的），搭了一台假服务器，在 TLS 握手中把这份证书发给你的浏览器。证书的签名、域名、有效期都没有问题。这次握手最终会在哪里露馅？

label.en: When the browser verifies the CA's signature on the certificate
label.zh: 浏览器验证证书上 CA 的签名时

feedback.en: The certificate is genuine and the CA's signature is entirely valid, so this check passes.
feedback.zh: 证书是真的，CA 的签名完全有效，这一关过得去。

label.en: When the browser checks the domain name on the certificate
label.zh: 浏览器核对证书域名时

feedback.en: The certificate says exactly www.unimelb.edu.au, so the name matches.
feedback.zh: 证书上写的正是 www.unimelb.edu.au，名字对得上。

label.en: The fake server has no private key, cannot decrypt the pre-master secret in Client Key Exchange, cannot compute the session key, and cannot send a Server Finished that passes the check
label.zh: 假服务器没有私钥，解不开 Client Key Exchange 里的预主密钥，算不出会话密钥，发不出能通过检验的 Server Finished

feedback.en: Right. A certificate only proves that the public key belongs to this name; whoever holds the private key is the real server.
feedback.zh: 对。证书只证明公钥属于这个名字，握着私钥的才是真服务器。

label.en: The algorithm list in Client Hello does not match the certificate
label.zh: Client Hello 里的算法清单和证书对不上

feedback.en: There is no such correspondence between the algorithm list and the certificate, and the fake server can simply pick any algorithm from the list.
feedback.zh: 算法清单和证书之间没有这种对应关系，假服务器完全可以从清单里选一个算法。

hints.en: Who is able to decrypt something encrypted with the server's public key?
hints.zh: 谁才有本事解开用服务器公钥加密的东西？

explain.en: A certificate proves “this public key belongs to this name”, not “whoever sent the certificate holds the private key”. The browser encrypts the pre-master secret with the public key in the certificate. Only the real server holding the private key can decrypt it, and only it can compute the session key and make a correct Server Finished. The fake server gives itself away here.
explain.zh: 证书证明“这把公钥属于这个名字”，不证明“发证书的人握着私钥”。浏览器把预主密钥用证书里的公钥加密。只有握着私钥的真服务器解得开，也只有它能算出会话密钥、做出正确的 Server Finished。假服务器到这里就露馅了。

title.en: IPsec or HTTPS: it depends on whom you protect
title.zh: IPsec 还是 HTTPS：看你要保护谁

text.en: Both use cryptography to protect communication, but they sit in different places and are used on different occasions.
text.zh: 两者都用密码学保护通信，但放的位置不同，用的场合也不同。

rows.en: Below HTTP and above TCP, chosen by the application
rows.zh: HTTP 之下、TCP 之上，应用选用

rows.en: All traffic between two hosts or two gateways, whatever the application
rows.zh: 两台主机、两个网关之间的所有流量，不管是哪个应用

rows.en: The connection of one application (the web)
System or gateway configuration; applications need not change
rows.zh: 系统或网关配置；应用不用改

rows.en: The application must support it (browsers and websites already do)
rows.zh: 应用要支持（浏览器和网站本来就支持）

rows.en: Agreed in advance: pre-shared key or certificate, SA built
rows.zh: 事先约好：预共享密钥或证书，建好 SA

rows.en: A stranger's site is fine: the browser has built-in CAs and verifies by certificate
rows.zh: 陌生网站也行：浏览器内置 CA，靠证书验明

rows.en: Linking branch offices, employees accessing the company network remotely (VPN)
rows.zh: 分公司互联、员工远程接入公司内网 (VPN)

rows.en: You open any website, online banking
rows.zh: 你打开任意一个网站、网上银行

text.en: Ask two questions when choosing. Is it all applications that need protecting, or one application? Is the other side known in advance, or a stranger met on the way? Between branch offices, or an employee back to the company network: the other side is known and all applications need protecting, so choose IPsec. You open any website: the other side is a stranger and only the web is protected, so choose HTTPS.
text.zh: 选的时候问两个问题。要保护的是所有应用，还是一个应用？对方是事先认识的，还是路上遇到的陌生人？分公司之间、员工回公司内网：对方认识，所有应用都要保护，选 IPsec。你打开任意一个网站：对方是陌生人，只保护网页，选 HTTPS。

title.en: Back to that click: who protects what along the way
title.zh: 回到那次点击：一路上谁在保护什么

text.en: You open www.unimelb.edu.au in your dorm. Every stage the browser goes through protects something different.
text.zh: 你在宿舍打开 www.unimelb.edu.au。浏览器一路走过的每一段，保护的东西都不一样。

head.en: What people along the way can see

rows.zh: DNS 问出 IP（第 14 课）

rows.en: You are looking up www.unimelb.edu.au; the DNS query from the course is in plaintext
rows.zh: 你在查 www.unimelb.edu.au，课上的 DNS 查询是明文
TCP 三次握手（第 12 课）

rows.en: Your IP connecting to their IP and port 443
rows.zh: 你的 IP 在连对方的 IP 和 443 端口

rows.en: Nobody: the IP header and TCP header are outside TLS
rows.zh: 没人：IP 头和 TCP 头在 TLS 之外

rows.en: The algorithm list and the certificate (the certificate is public anyway)
rows.zh: 算法清单和证书（证书本来就公开）

rows.en: TLS: the certificate and Finished verify the server; the session key is safely built with the public key
rows.zh: TLS：证书和 Finished 验明服务器，会话密钥由公钥安全建立
HTTP 请求与网页（第 15 课）

rows.en: Only ciphertext: path, cookies and page content cannot be read
rows.zh: 只有密文：路径、cookie、页面内容都读不出

rows.en: TLS: symmetric encryption plus integrity check
rows.zh: TLS：对称加密加完整性校验

rows.en: Campus network exit (if there is a firewall)
rows.zh: 校园网出口（如果有防火墙）

rows.en: The firewall allows or denies by address and port
rows.zh: 防火墙按地址和端口放行或拒绝

rows.en: Connecting from home to the school's internal systems
Outsiders see only the tunnel between two gateways
rows.zh: 外人只看到两个网关之间的隧道

text.en: Two things are worth remembering. HTTPS protects the page content, but does not hide “where you went”: the DNS query and the destination IP are still in plaintext. Each measure handles only its own layer and its own few properties, so a secure visit is really several layers of measures stacked together.
text.zh: 两件事值得记住。HTTPS 保护了页面内容，但没有藏起“你去了哪里”：DNS 查询和目的 IP 仍然是明文。每个措施只管它那一层、那几条性质，所以一次安全的访问，其实是几层措施叠在一起。

title.en: Given a threat, pick the right measure
title.zh: 给一种威胁，选对措施

prompt.en: Of the following four “threat → measure” pairs, which is correct?
prompt.zh: 下面四组“威胁 → 措施”，哪一组配对是对的？

label.en: Two branch offices send plaintext data over the Internet with an old program that cannot be modified → build an IPsec tunnel between the two branches' gateways
label.zh: 两个分公司用一个没法修改的老程序在互联网上传明文数据 → 在两个分公司的网关之间建 IPsec 隧道

feedback.en: Right. IPsec protects all applications at once at the network layer, and the old program does not need a single line changed.
feedback.zh: 对。IPsec 在网络层一次保护所有应用，老程序一行代码也不用改。

label.en: Someone sets up a fake website that looks like the bank's → install a firewall at the internal network border
label.zh: 有人搭了一个和银行长得一样的假网站 → 在内网边界装防火墙

feedback.en: A firewall allows by address and port and cannot tell a real website from a fake one. Verifying the server takes the certificate and handshake in HTTPS.
feedback.zh: 防火墙按地址和端口放行，认不出网站的真假。验明服务器要靠 HTTPS 里的证书和握手。

label.en: A customer later denies sending that order → encrypt the transmission with IPsec or HTTPS
label.zh: 客户事后否认自己发过那份订单 → 用 IPsec 或 HTTPS 加密传输

feedback.en: They protect data with keys shared by both sides, and anyone can produce the same checksum, so they cannot prove who sent it. Non-repudiation takes a digital signature.
feedback.zh: 它们保护数据用的是双方共享的密钥，谁都做得出同样的校验码，证明不了是谁发的。不可否认要靠数字签名。

label.en: A website is crushed by a flood of junk requests and users cannot open it → add an HMAC to every packet
label.zh: 网站被海量垃圾请求拖垮，用户打不开 → 给每个包加 HMAC

feedback.en: An HMAC is about integrity: finding out that a packet was altered. The junk requests were not altered and can still crush the service. For availability, of these four kinds of solution only the firewall partly helps.
feedback.zh: HMAC 管的是完整性：发现包被改过。垃圾请求本身没被改，照样能把服务压垮。可用性这条，这四类方案里只有防火墙部分地管。

explain.en: a is right: the tunnel encrypts uniformly at the network layer, and the old program need not change. b: authenticating the website takes a certificate, and a firewall only governs what goes in and out at the border. c: non-repudiation takes a digital signature, which neither IPsec nor TLS provides. d: an HMAC protects integrity, not availability.
explain.zh: a 对：隧道在网络层统一加密，老程序不用改。b：认证网站靠证书，防火墙只管边界上的进出。c：不可否认要靠数字签名，IPsec 和 TLS 都不提供。d：HMAC 保完整性，不保可用性。
